original_question: Given a closed convex curve gamma, let G(gamma, l) denote the outer curve produced by the string or gardener construction with string length l > |gamma|. If this construction is transitive in the sense that for ellipses one has G(G(gamma_1, l_1), l_2) = G(gamma_1, l_3) for a unique l_3, are ellipses the only closed convex curves that satisfy this transitivity property?
target_in_paper: §5.1, Problem 1b: "Ellipses are the only closed convex curves satisfying the above transitivity." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right construction, the right object G(γ,ℓ), the key transitivity relation G(G(γ1,ℓ1),ℓ2)=G(γ1,ℓ3), the uniqueness of ℓ3, and the intended exclusivity question about ellipses. That is exactly the content of the official Problem 1b in §5.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
missing_details: The paper works with a closed convex curve γ in R^2, and |γ| denotes its perimeter. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))

G(γ,ℓ) should be defined as the closed convex curve obtained by the string (gardener) construction that contains γ in its interior, not just informally as an 'outer curve.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))

To make 'satisfying the above transitivity' fully stand-alone, the quantifiers should be explicit: for every admissible first length ℓ1>|γ| and every admissible second length ℓ2>|G(γ,ℓ1)|, there exists a unique admissible ℓ3>|γ| with G(G(γ,ℓ1),ℓ2)=G(γ,ℓ3). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
The second admissibility condition ℓ2>|G(γ,ℓ1)| is part of the nearby statement in the paper and is missing from the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
The official problem does not impose extra smoothness or strict-convexity assumptions here; it asks about closed convex curves as such. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))

The paper presents this as a geometric variant suggested by the Birkhoff conjecture, not as a proved equivalent reformulation, so the refined version should not state or imply equivalence with Problem 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
refined_question: Let γ⊂R^2 be a closed convex curve, let |γ| denote its perimeter, and for each ℓ>|γ| let G(γ,ℓ) be the closed convex curve containing γ in its interior obtained by the string (gardener) construction. Say that γ satisfies the transitivity property if for every ℓ1>|γ| and every ℓ2>|G(γ,ℓ1)| there exists a unique ℓ3>|γ| such that G(G(γ,ℓ1),ℓ2)=G(γ,ℓ3). Are ellipses the only closed convex curves satisfying this transitivity property? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at §5.1, Problem 1b rather than the main Birkhoff conjecture itself, because it uses the paper’s string/gardener construction G(c,ℓ) and the immediately preceding ellipse-specific transitivity statement as its starting point. In the nearby context, the paper defines G(c,ℓ) for ℓ>|c|, notes that if Y(c,ℓ) is the billiard table bounded by G(c,ℓ) then c is a caustic for the billiard on Y(c,ℓ), and then states the transitivity property for ellipses before posing Problem 1b. The refinement therefore keeps the question exactly at that geometric open problem, while adding only the missing ambient space, perimeter notation, and universal quantifiers needed to make 'the above transitivity' self-contained. The survey also frames Problem 1b as an 'entirely geometric variant' suggested by Problem 1, not as an explicitly proved equivalent formulation, so no alternate equivalent question should be supplied. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))
